subject: Request: Temporary SLA handover & response carveout for regional maintenance
messages:
From: Alice Kim <alice.kim@northstream.co>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops-eng+oncall@northstream.co
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Temporary SLA window: planned overnight maintenance (Apr 22-24)

Hi Irene,

Quick note from NorthStream ops: we have a regional networking maintenance window for our US-west edge (SFO) scheduled for Apr 22 23:00 - Apr 24 06:00 PT. The maintenance will involve routing changes and may increase tail latency for requests that hit the SFO edge.

We rely on Redwood's P1/P2 response commitments for production incidents and want to understand whether a temporary carveout/hand-over for overnight on-call routing is required so we don't trip contractual SLOs.

Can you confirm:
- Whether Redwood can route affected traffic to another region automatically during that window, and if not, what temporary changes to our P1/P2 response expectations you recommend?
- If an SLA carveout is needed, what specific time ranges / metrics would be excluded and what approvals you need from our side?

We'd like to handle this by Friday so procurement/ops can sign off. Attaching the maintenance summary from our side.

Thanks,
Alice Kim
Senior Reliability Engineer, NorthStream
attachments: northstream_maintenance_summary.pdf
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Kim <alice.kim@northstream.co>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Temporary SLA window: planned overnight maintenance (Apr 22-24)

Hi Alice — thanks for the heads up and the summary.

Short answer: we can support a temporary exception, but we need to confirm impact and align on an operational handover. A few follow-ups from our side so we can scope the carveout precisely:
1) Expected % of traffic to SFO during that window (peak tokens/min or requests/min).
2) Whether NorthStream can tolerate increased P1 response window to 3 hours overnight for the maintenance nights (we typically commit to 60min for P1, 4 hours for P2 in your contract).
3) If you want automatic regional failover or manual routing changes — automatic failover depends on cross-region capacity reservations.

I've attached a quick impact template — please populate if possible. I'm looping in Ben & Monica from Support/Customer Success to propose an on-call coverage plan and escalation path while the maintenance is in effect.

Irene Choi
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
attachments: SLA_impact_analysis_NorthStream_Apr2028.xlsx
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Apr 2028 08:16:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Temporary SLA window: planned overnight maintenance (Apr 22-24)

Irene / Monica — quick internal coordination:

Summary of our constraints:
- Our us-east pool has burst headroom but is committed across other customers that night; can't guarantee sustained failover at full TPS without a short-notice capacity bump.
- We can implement prefix KV-routing to push NorthStream requests away from SFO for high-priority routes if they can provide request routing keys.
- For P1/P2 response timing: I'm comfortable proposing an overnight P1 response window of 120 minutes (for Apr 22 & 23 nights only) and maintain P2 at 4 hours. This is conditional on NorthStream enabling automatic failover for non-stateful requests.

Proposed escalation path during maintenance:
1) Operations alert -> NorthStream on-call (existing) + Redwood on-call (primary) -> 30m to acknowledge.
2) If unacknowledged -> Redwood SRE rotation lead (Ben) -> 45m to engage mitigation.
3) If cross-region capacity needed -> Infra urgent capacity request to Capacity Ops (Marissa looped).

I can draft a short playbook. Attaching our on-call matrix for review.

Ben
Principal Support Engineer, Redwood Inference
attachments: oncall_matrix_redwood.pdf
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Apr 2028 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Temporary SLA window: planned overnight maintenance (Apr 22-24)

Couple of practical notes before we reply to NorthStream:
- If we propose a 120m P1 overnight, we should add a credit formula for any missed P1s during the carveout (pro-rated by incident count) to avoid downstream billing disputes.
- Ask NorthStream to sign a one-page amendment (term + start/end times + fallback routing behavior). I can help with legal language.
- Recommend we include a triage video call during the first maintenance night at 00:30 PT to validate routing and visibility.

Draft playbook outline I'm pushing to Confluence. Once you sign off, Irene, we'll send the proposal to Alice and procurement.

-M
Marissa Cole
Head of Support Operations
Redwood Inference
attachments: proposed_playbook_northstream.md
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Kim <alice.kim@northstream.co>, ops-eng+oncall@northstream.co
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Apr 2028 16:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Temporary SLA window: planned overnight maintenance (Apr 22-24) — Proposal and ask

Hi Alice — thanks for the patience. Based on your maintenance summary and our capacity check, here's Redwood's proposal for the Apr 22 & 23 overnight maintenance window: 

1) Temporary SLA carveout (approved):
   - P1 response window adjusted to 120 minutes for the nights of Apr 22 23:00 -> Apr 23 06:00 PT and Apr 23 23:00 -> Apr 24 06:00 PT only.
   - P2 unchanged at 4 hours.
   - Exclusion applies only to latency-induced P1s where request routing to SFO is impacted; availability incidents (complete service outage) remain covered by standard SLAs.

2) Operational controls and conditions:
   - NorthStream provides expected traffic profile (requests/min) no later than Apr 18 17:00 PT using the attached SLA_impact_analysis template.
   - NorthStream enables automatic failover for non-stateful endpoints OR agrees to the 120m P1 window.
   - Redwood will run a verification call at 00:30 PT on Apr 23 to validate routing.

3) Escalation path (during carveout):
   - Primary: NorthStream on-call -> Redwood on-call (ack within 30m).
   - Secondary: Redwood SRE rotation lead (Ben Carter) -> engage mitigation within 45m.
   - Tertiary: Redwood Infra Capacity Ops (Marissa) for emergency cross-region capacity; this may be subject to one-time capacity fees if sustained.

4) Credits and sign-off:
   - Any P1 credits triggered during the carveout will be pro-rated: 0.5x standard P1 credit per missed P1 incident that is demonstrably caused by SFO routing maintenance.
   - Please confirm acceptance and provide the traffic profile by Apr 18 EOD. We'll prepare a one-page amendment for signatures once you confirm.

If this works, Monica and I will coordinate the amendment and the verification call.

Thanks — Irene
Irene Choi
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
